Col. i 25; in Eph. i 23 the Messiah is being fulfilled (completed) by the Church.

προσέρχομαι.s: προσέρχομαι, I come up to, I come to; I come near (to), I approach; I consent (to), 1 Tim. vi 3.

προσεύχομαι.s: προσεύχομαι, I pray; c. acc., I pray for: sometimes with Hebraistic tautology, προσευχῇ or διὰ προσευχῆς is added.

ὥστε.mg: as, like as; conj., so as, that, so that
ὥστε.s: ὥστε, (a) with an infinitive, expressing result, so as to, Lk. iv 29 (v. l.), ix 52 (v. l.), xx 20 (v. l.), &c.; (b) introducing an independent clause, in indic., imper., subjunct. of exhortation, so that, John iii 16, Gal. ii 13; with result stated merely as a new fact, consequently, and so, therefore.

αἰτέω.s: αἰτέω, I ask, request, beg, petition: middle voice αἰτέομαι, I ask for myself (perhaps with entreaty).

ἀποκτείνω.s: ἀποκτείνω, ἀποκτέννω, ἀποκτεννύω (absent from papyri of N.T. times), I kill.

ἀπόστολος.s: ἀπόστολος, a messenger, an envoy, a delegate, one commissioned by another to represent him in some way, especially a man sent out by Jesus Christ Himself to preach the Gospel, an apostle.

βαπτίζω.s: βαπτίζω, lit. I dip, submerge, but specifically of ceremonial dipping (whether immersion or affusion), I baptize; when the preposition εἰς with a noun in the accus. follows, it appears to indicate that through this ceremony the baptized person becomes the property of the person indicated after εἰς: met. Mk. x 38.

δίκαιος.mg: just, right. οὐ δίκαιός εἰμι, I ought not
δίκαιος.s: δίκαιος, just; especially, just in the eyes of God, righteous: οἱ δίκαιοι in Mt. the elect (a Jewish idea): κρίνω τὸ δίκαιον, I give just judgement, Lk. xii 57.

δώδεκα.s: δώδεκα, twelve: οἱ δώδεκα, the usual way in which the Twelve disciples of Jesus are referred to.

ἑπτά.s: ἑπτά, seven: οἱ ἑπτά, the seven (‘deacons’ of Ac. vi 3–6).

εὐαγγέλιον.g: the good news (of the coming of the Messiah), the Gospel
εὐαγγέλιον.s: εὐαγγέλιον, τό, the good news of the coming of the Messiah, the gospel: the gen. after it expresses sometimes the giver (God), sometimes the subject (the Messiah, &c.), sometimes the human transmitter (an apostle).

καταβαίνω.mg: to go down, descend, to go down from Babylon to the seacoast
καταβαίνω.s: καταβαίνω, I go down, I come down, either from the sky or from higher land.

κεφαλή.s: κεφαλή, (a) head, κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων, see κατά; (b) met. κεφαλὴ γωνίας, a corner stone, uniting two walls, Mk. xii 10 and parallels; head, ruler, lord, 1 Cor. xi 3, &c.

μαρτυρέω.s: μαρτυρέω, I witness, I bear witness, I give evidence, I testify, c. dat. pers. or quality, in one’s favour, in favour of; c. acc. cognate, μαρτυρίαν, ὁμολογίαν, practically otiose; in the passive, I am witnessed to, I am borne witness to, sometimes with nom. and dependent infin. (impersonal, 3 John 12), corresponding to the act.; Rev. i 2, xxii 16, 18, 20.

πονηρός.mg: wretched, wicked. ὁ πονηρός, the wretch
πονηρός.s: πονηρός (malignus), evil, wicked, malicious, particularly as active: especially, ὁ πονηρός (even Mt. vi 13, [Lk. xi 4], according to the almost unanimous opinion of the early Church), the evil one, i.e. Satan, the devil (a Hebraism); many passages like these, being in the oblique cases, are unfortunately ambiguous, but Mt. xiii 19, 1 John ii 13, 14, v 18 are absolutely certain examples of the masculine, and in many other passages there is a strong probability: τὸ πονηρόν, the evil in the world, all that is wicked, e.g. Rom. xii 9.

πρόσωπον.d: prosopography, description of the face or personal appearance
πρόσωπον.s: πρόσωπον, (a) the human face; often Hebraistically otiose, e.g. πρὸ προσώπου σου practically = πρὸ σοῦ, Mt. xi 10; πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον (Hebraistic), face to face; (b) hence applied to God, from His having been originally conceived as in human form, presence (cf. Ac. v 41); (c) appearance, outward aspect (Mt. xvi 3), Lk. xii 56, &c.; surface, Lk. xxi 35; (d) for the practically synonymous Hebraistic expressions βλέπειν εἰς πρόσωπον, θαυμάζειν πρόσωπον, λαμβάνειν πρόσωπον, to show special favour to, see under λαμβάνω; (e) by Hebraistic pleonasm (cf. (a) above), πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ, before his entrance, Ac. xiii 24; (f) person in a rather loose sense as a possessor of dignity or honour; pride, James i 11.

πῦρ.s: πῦρ, fire; a fire, both literally, and metaphorically, and eschatologically (as an instrument of punishment in the conception of later Judaism, the fire of the Divine wrath which burns in Gehenna).

σημεῖον.s: σημεῖον (signum), a sign, an outward (visible) indication of secret power or truth; a miracle regarded from that point of view.

στόμα.s: στόμα, the mouth, especially as an organ of speech in man and God: the sword has a mouth (edge), because it drinks blood, Lk. xxi 24, Heb. xi 34: στόμα πρὸς στόμα (cf. πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον), by word of mouth, practically, face to face.

τηρέω.s: τηρέω, (a) lit. I watch, observe; (b) I guard, preserve, keep, protect; (c) of commandments and regulations, I observe, keep, obey.

ὕδωρ.s: ὕδωρ, water: ὕδωρ ζῶν (aqua uiua), ζωῆς (Hebraistic genitive), flowing water (as opposed to stagnant), John iv 10, &c.

ὑπάγω.s: ὑπάγω, I go away, withdraw, depart; I depart this life, Mt. xxvi 24.

φῶς.s: φῶς, a light, particularly the light of the sun, but also the heavenly bodies specially, James i 17: as indispensable to life, it comes to be associated with life (cf. John i 4), and as universal beneficence, with God and the Messiah (cf. John i 8, viii 12), &c. (cf. John xii 36, Eph. v 8): τὸ φῶς, the (bright) fire, Mk. xiv 54, Lk. xxii 56.

χαίρω.mg: to rejoice, be glad; χαῖρε, hail, farewell
χαίρω.s: χαίρω, (a) I rejoice, c. cognate acc. or c. dat., I rejoice exceedingly; (b) in the imperative, χαῖρε, χαίρετε, a greeting, farewell, Christianised in Phil. iii 1, iv 4 bis, by the addition ἐν κυρίῳ (and generally mistranslated), cf. χαίρειν, imperatival infin., e.g. Ac. xv 23 (cf. 2 John 10); also hail! Mk. xv 18, Mt. xxvii 29.

ἀγαπητός.s: ἀγαπητός, loved, beloved, with two special applications, (a) ὁ ἀγαπητός, the Beloved, a title of the Messiah (Christ), as beloved beyond all others by the God who sent Him; (b) of Christians, as beloved by God, Christ, and one another.

ἄγω.mg: 2 ao. ἤγαγον, ἦχα, ἦγμαι, ἤχθην, to lead, bring, live
ἄγω.s: ἄγω, (a) I lead, I lead away, I bring (a person, or animal); thus I bring before a court of justice; (b) especially in 1st pers. plur. subjunct. ἄγωμεν, intr. let us depart (e.g. Mk. i 38); (c) I hold, keep, celebrate: ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται (Ac. xix 38), assizes are held.

αἰώνιος.s: αἰώνιος, (a) age-long, and, therefore, practically eternal, unending; (b) partaking of the character of that which lasts for an age, as contrasted with that which is brief and fleeting.

ἀπολύω.s: ἀπολύω (dimitto), I let loose, set free, release, permit to depart: middle, I withdraw myself, depart, Ac. xxviii 25.

γραμματεύς.s: γραμματεύς, (a) in Jerusalem, a scribe, one learned in the Jewish Law, a religious teacher; (b) at Ephesus, the town-clerk, the secretary of the city, Ac. xix 35.

δοκέω.d: Docetism, the early heresy that Christ's body was phantasmal or of celestial substance which merely seemed human
δοκέω.s: δοκέω (uideor), I seem, am thought; δοκεῖ impers. c. dat. (placet), it seems good, it is resolved by.

ἔξω.s: ἔξω, (a) adv. without; in ὁ ἔξω, &c. the adv. is equivalent to an adjective, τὰς ἔξω πόλεις, foreign cities, Ac. xxvi 11, ὁ ἔξω ἄνθρωπος, the outer (physical) nature, 2 Cor. iv 16, especially οἱ ἔξω, the outsiders, the non-Christians; (b) prep. c. gen. outside.

θέλημα.d: Monothelite, one who holds that Christ had but one will, the divine; condemned by the Sixth General Council, A.D. 680
θέλημα.s: θέλημα, an act of will, will; plur. wishes, desires; τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, the will of God, sometimes as a will to be recognized, sometimes as a will to be obeyed.

ἱμάτιον.s: ἱμάτιον, a long flowing outer garment.

καρπός.s: καρπός (fructus), (a) fruit, generally vegetable, sometimes animal (e.g. Lk. i 42, Ac. ii 30); (b) met. fruit, deed, action, result, Mt. iii 8, Lk. iii 8, James iii 17 f., &c.; (c) profit, gain, Rom. i 13, &c.

κηρύσσω.g: I proclaim (as a herald, κῆρυξ), preach

νύξ.s: νύξ, (a) night: νυκτός, διὰ νυκτός, by night, sometime during the night, see also ἡμέρα; (b) met. 1 Thess. v 5, &c.

ὄρος.d: orology, the scientific study of mountains

οὔτε.s: οὔτε: οὔτε... οὔτε, neither... nor; οὐ... οὔτε... οὔτε, not... neither... nor; sometimes the other clause is positive, e.g. John iv 11, 3 John 10.

πιστός.s: πιστός, faithful, trusty, trustworthy, reliable: οἱ πιστοί, the Christians.

πλοῖον.s: πλοῖον, a boat; hence a ship (the old word ναῦς having become almost obsolete), Ac. xx 13, &c.

πρεσβύτερος.s: πρεσβύτερος, (a) of age simply, the elder of two, Lk. xv 25; old, aged, Ac. ii 17, 1 Tim. v 1; plur. our (their, &c.) ancestors, Mt. xv 2, Mk. vii 3, 5, Heb. xi 2; (b) a title of honour applied among the Jews to various classes of dignitary, because such offices were originally conferred on the old, e.g. a member of the Sanhedrin, Mt. xvi 21, &c., [τοῦ Ἰσραήλ], Ac. iv 8, τῶν Ἰουδαίων, Ac. xxv 15, τοῦ λαοῦ, Mt. xxi 23, &c.: magistrates of a particular city, Lk. vii 3; (c) among the Christians, an elder of a congregation or church, Ac. xi 30, &c., τῆς ἐκκλησίας, Ac. xx 17, James v 14, one of whom was commonly appointed ἐπίσκοπος; hence the two words are practically identical in meaning, the former indicating status, the latter function; (d) an elder of the twenty-four in the heavenly assembly, Rev. iv 4, &c. [The title was applied in Egypt (a) to holders of a communal office in civil life, who were responsible for the peace of the village, and received a small salary, (b) to priests of pagan temples.]

ῥῆμα.s: ῥῆμα, (a) a spoken word, an utterance, the concrete expression of λόγος: hence, perhaps Hebraistically, (b) a subject as spoken about, a subject of speech, a matter, a thing, a fact, Mt. xviii 16, Lk. i 37, ii 15, &c.; (c) in a solemn sense, of a divine word, Lk. iii 2, Eph. vi 17, &c.; (d) the Christian teaching, the gospel, 1 Pet. i 25 bis (cf. Rom. x 8 ff.), (the first = the promise to deliver Israel); (e) the Christian confession, ‘Jesus is Lord’, which leads to salvation, and precedes baptism, Eph. v 26, cf. Rom. x 9, 1 Cor. xii 3, Phil. ii 11.

σάββατον.s: σάββατον (Semitic), sing. and plur., the Sabbath, a night and day which lasted from about 6 p.m. on Friday till about 6 p.m. on Saturday: πρώτη (μία) [τῶν] σαββάτων ([τοῦ] σαββάτου) (Hebraistic), the first day after the Sabbath, the day following the Sabbath, that is, from about 6 p.m. on Saturday till about 6 p.m. on Sunday, Sunday.

συνάγω.s: συνάγω, I gather together, collect, assemble, persons or things: συναγαγὼν πάντα implies the converting of the goods into money, having sold all off, Lk. xv 13.

τρεῖς.s: τρεῖς, three; μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας = τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

φέρω.mg: to BEAR, carry, bring, endure, produce, lead, accomplish. χαλεπῶς or κακῶς φέρομαι, I take it ill
φέρω.s: φέρω (fero), I carry, bear, bring; I conduct, lead, both tr. and intr.; perhaps, I make publicly known, Heb. ix 16.

ὧδε.s: ὧδε, here, both of rest and of motion to (hither): τὰ ὧδε, the things here, what is here, what is going on here, the state of affairs here.

ἀρχή.s: ἀρχή, (a) rule (kingly or magisterial); (b) plur., in a quasi-personal sense, almost rulers, magistrates, Tit. iii 1; (c) beginning: in the very difficult John viii 25 τὴν ἀρχήν would naturally mean originally, but the passage is not yet explained.

ἀσπάζομαι.s: ἀσπάζομαι (saluto, a term regularly used at the end of a letter), I greet, salute; I pay my respects to, Ac. xxv 13.

δοξάζω.s: δοξάζω, I glorify, bestow glory on: τὸν θεόν, I acknowledge the glory of God.

ἐπερωτάω.s: ἐπερωτάω = ἐρωτάω simply, I ask, question.

ἐρωτάω.s: ἐρωτάω, (a) I ask (a question), I question; (b) (= αἰτέω) I request, make a request to; I pray.

ἤδη.s: ἤδη, already; now at length, now after all this waiting Rom. i 10.

λοιπός.g: remaining; as a noun, the rest; as an adverb, for the rest, henceforth
λοιπός.mg: left, remaining. ὁ λοιπός, the remainder
λοιπός.s: λοιπός (reliquus), (a) left, left behind, οἱ λοιποί, the remainder, the rest, the others; (b) adverbial phrases, acc. neut., λοιπόν, τὸ λοιπόν, for the rest, now, already; temporal gen., τοῦ λοιποῦ (sc. χρόνου), henceforth.

μέσος.d: Mesopotamia, in the midst of the rivers [Tigris and Euphrates]
μέσος.s: μέσος, middle, in the middle, sometimes followed by the genitive of the whole area referred to; adverbial (with or without gen.) are μέσον (acc. neut.), ἀνὰ μέσον (elliptical in 1 Cor. vi 5), κατὰ μέσον, ἐν [τῷ] μέσῳ, in the middle, before them all, ἐκ μέσου, from the midst.

οὐχί.s: οὐχί, a more emphatic form of οὐ (οὐκ, οὐχ), not; no, not so; also = nonne, in a question, expecting a positive answer.

πλείων.mg: much, many. adv., πολύ, πολλά. οἱ πολλοί, the majority
πλείων.s: πολύς (compar. πλείων and superl. πλεῖστος, which see), a word indicating quantity and number, not size, sing. much, plur. many: οἱ πολλοί (plerique), the majority: πολλῷ (multo), before a comparative, much: πολλά, as adv., much (often in Mk., an exact translation of Aramaic), like the more regular πολύ: πολλοῦ (magni), for much, at a great price, Mt. xxvi 9: with sing. words indicating time, long is the most suitable English rendering: πολλάς (sc. πληγάς), Lk. xii 47. The καί following, Ac. xxv 7, is superfluous according to our idiom.

προσκυνέω.s: προσκυνέω, I go down on my knees to; I do obeisance to; I worship.

συναγωγή.s: συναγωγή (in origin abstract, a leading [bringing] together, convening an assembly, then concrete, a [religious] meeting), a meeting (assembly), a place of meeting (assembly), particularly of Jews for the reading of scripture and for worship, a synagogue. In certain passages it is doubtful whether the congregation (e.g. John vi 59, xviii 20) or the place of meeting (e.g. James ii 2) is particularly intended, but the sense is not seriously affected by the doubt. In the O.T. συναγωγή and ἐκκλησία are practically synonymous, but in ordinary Christian writings the former is rarely used, and seemingly only of communities of Jews or Jewish Christians (e.g. James ii 2, where it is probably the building).

τοιοῦτος.s: τοιοῦτος (talis), of such a kind (character), such.

ὑπάρχω.g: I am, exist; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, one's belongings
ὑπάρχω.s: ὑπάρχω, I am, denoting originally a state or condition still subsisting in contrast to what is temporary or accidental: τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, one’s belongings, possessions, personal property.

φημί.mg: φήσω (these parts are sometimes added: fut. ἐρῶ, aor. εἶπον, perf. εἴρηκα, p. mid. εἴρημαι, aor. pass. ἐρρήθην), to say, speak, affirm, assert; οὔ φημι, I deny

ἄχρι.g: with the gen., as far as, up to; as a conjunction, until
ἄχρι.s: ἄχρι, ἄχρις, as far as, up to, until; ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν = adhuc; ἄχρι οὗ (with or without ἄν) with the subjunctive, until.

γλῶσσα.d: glossolalia, the gift of speaking [cf. λαλεῖν] in tongues, I Cor. 14
γλῶσσα.s: γλῶσσα, (a) tongue, especially as an organ of speech; (b) tongue, language; (c) also, usually in the plural, for the unintelligible sounds uttered in spiritual ecstasy.

γραφή.d: Hagiographa, books of the Hebrew Scriptures not included under Law and Prophets
γραφή.s: γραφή, (a) a writing; (b) a passage of scripture: plur. αἱ γραφαί, the scriptures (of the Old Testament, and in 2 Pet. iii 16 also of the New).

δεξιός.mg: right. ἐν δεξιᾷ, on the right hand
δεξιός.s: δεξιός, on the right hand, right hand, right.

διό.s: διό (= δι’ ὅ, on account of which thing), wherefore.

ἔσχατος.s: ἔσχατος (ultimus), last: ἔσχατον, neut. acc. as adv., at the last, finally; ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου, at the end; ἕως ἐσχάτου, till the end.

εὐαγγελίζω.g: I bring good news, preach good tidings (the Gospel)
εὐαγγελίζω.s: εὐαγγελίζω, but far oftener mid. εὐαγγελίζομαι, I bring good news, I preach good tidings, with or without an obj., expressing either the persons who receive the good news or the good news itself (the good news being sometimes expressed as a person, e.g. Ac. v 42).

εὐθύς.s: εὐθύς, adv. immediately: characteristic of Mk.

λίθος.s: λίθος, a stone: met. of Jesus as the chief stone in a building, &c., Ac. iv 11, &c.

μηδέ.mg: but not, and not, μηδέ... μηδέ, neither... nor; adv., not even
μηδέ.s: μηδέ (neue, neque), generally after a preceding μή, nor... either.

μόνος.s: μόνος, alone: κατὰ μόνας = κατ’ ἰδίαν, by himself.

ὅπως.s: ὅπως, with the subjunctive, with or without ἄν, in order that; that (especially after ἐρωτάω).

παιδίον.s: παιδίον, (a) a little boy, a child (from birth onwards); hence affectionately, of those grown up; (b) (compare the use of boy in parts of Africa) a slave, Lk. xi 7 (according to an interpretation in Augustine).

παραβολή.s: παραβολή, a similitude, allegory, parable, emblematic allusion: in Heb. xi 19 ἐν = as.

πείθω.mg: to persuade; mid. and pass., obey
πείθω.s: πείθω, (a) (suadeo) I urge, I apply persuasion, I seek to persuade, I exercise suasion; (b) 2 perf. and pluperf., I trust, ἐπί, in; (c) mid. or pass. (I admit suasion to myself), I am persuaded; hence, I believe: hence also, c. dat., I obey.

σοφία.s: σοφία, wisdom, the highest intellectual gift, of comprehensive insight into the ways and purposes of God; sometimes, e.g. Ac. vi 3, 1 Cor. vi 5, James i 5, (prudentia) practical wisdom, that endowment of heart and mind which is needed for the right conduct of life.

χρόνος.s: χρόνος, time; a time, period: locative, πολλοῖς χρόνοις, oftentimes, Lk. viii 29, but instrumental, Lk. viii 27, Rom. xvi 25.

ἁμαρτωλός.g: sinful; as a noun, a sinner
ἁμαρτωλός.s: ἁμαρτωλός, (a) sinning, sinful; (b) frequent as a translation of a contemptuous Aramaic word, with reference to particular classes despised by strict Jews, a sinner.

ἀπαγγέλλω.s: ἀπαγγέλλω, I report (from one place to another), I bring a report, I announce.

ἀποδίδωμι.g: I give back, pay; middle, I sell
ἀποδίδωμι.s: ἀποδίδωμι (reddo), (a) I give back, return, restore; (b) I give, render, as due; (c) middle, I sell, Ac. v 8, &c.

ἄρα.s: ἄρα, an inferential particle, then, therefore: found also in combination with other particles, such as γε and οὖν, &c.; εἰ ἄρα (si forte), if perchance, Mk. xi 13, &c.

ἔμπροσθεν.g: with the gen., in front of, before
ἔμπροσθεν.s: ἔμπροσθεν, in front, before the face: sometimes made a substantive by the addition of the article; usually c. gen. in front of, before the face of.

ἔρημος.g: solitary, deserted; as a noun, ἡ ἔρημος, the desert, wilderness
ἔρημος.s: ἔρημος (the Latin heremus may be due to false analogy with heres, hereticus, &c.), adj. desert; hence, ἡ ἔρημος (sc. χώρα), the desert, to the E. and S. of Palestine: of a person, deserted, abandoned, desolate, Gal. iv 27.

ἔτος.d: the Etesian winds in the Mediterranean region blow annually
ἔτος.s: ἔτος, ἕτος, a year: κατ’ ἔτος (καθ’ ἕτος), annually; ἀπὸ or ἐξ ἐτῶν followed by a number (Fr. depuis, Germ. seit, English for), lit. from... years.

καθίζω.d: cf. cathedral, properly, the church which contains the bishop's chair or seat
καθίζω.s: καθίζω, (a) tr. I make to sit, I set; (b) intr. aor. I sat down.

κακός.s: κακός, bad, evil, in the widest sense.

κρατέω.s: κρατέω, I lay hold of, take possession of, obtain, c. gen. and (much oftener) c. acc.

κρίσις.s: κρίσις, judging, judgement; generally divine judgement: accusation, Jude 9.

μικρός.s: μικρός, (a) small: superl. μικρότερος, smallest, in Mk. xv 40 possibly junior; (b) of time, short; see μικρόν.

παραλαμβάνω.s: παραλαμβάνω, I take from, I receive from, or, I take to, I receive (apparently not used of money, see ἀπέχω); I take with me.

ποῦ.s: ποῦ, where?: also used (for the obsolete ποῖ) in the sense, whither?, to what place?

πρό.mg: prep. with gen., before, on account of; πρὸ τοῦ, before this, formerly
πρό.s: πρό, (a) of place, before, in front of; (b) of time, before, earlier than; found even with article and the infinitive = πρίν: πρὸ ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ πάσχα, six days before, &c., John xii 1, πρὸ ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων, fourteen years before, 2 Cor. xii 2.

προσφέρω.mg: to present; pass., w. fut. mid., attack
προσφέρω.s: προσφέρω, (a) I bring to; (b) characteristically, I offer (of gifts, sacrifices, &c.).

σπείρω.s: σπείρω, I sow, lit. or met.

σωτηρία.s: σωτηρία (in extra-Biblical language [= salus] has a reference generally to bodily health, welfare [so also Ac. xxvii 34, Heb. xi 7], especially as recovered after illness, but also to deliverance from every calamity, victory over enemies), the salvation to be wrought by the Messiah for the Jews, the release from the foreign yoke in particular and the recovery of independence (cf. John iv 22): in purely Christian terminology, far fuller in content, including complete recovery of health from the disease of sin, release from captivity to it.

τρίτος.s: τρίτος (see also τρίτον), third: ἐκ τρίτου, a third time: τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ (according to the ancient method of counting), on the third day, two days after, on the next day but one, on the day after to-morrow.

τυφλός.s: τυφλός, blind, either lit. or met.

φόβος.s: φόβος, fear, terror, often fear on the reverential side, in reference to God, and such as inspires cautious dealing towards men, cf. 1 Pet. i 17.

φυλακή.g: a guard, a prison, a watch
φυλακή.s: φυλακή, (a) (custodia) abstract, guardianship, guard, in cognate acc., Lk. ii 8, Ac. xii 6; (b) (custodia) a guard, Ac. xii 10; (c) much commoner, a prison; hence, the place of confinement of the spirits of the dead, 1 Pet. iii 19; (d) (uigilia), as a division of the night, (1) perhaps according to the old Jewish system by which there were three divisions, Lk. xii 38, (2) according to the Roman system, popularized in Judaea, by which there were four, Mk. vi 48 (cf. xiii 35), Mt. xiv 25, xxiv 43.

χρεία.s: χρεία, need; any special occasion or matter in hand, Ac. vi 3, Eph. iv 29 (?).

ἁμαρτάνω.d: cf. hamartialogy, the doctrine of sin
ἁμαρτάνω.mg: 2 ao. ἥμαρτον, ἡμάρτηκα, etc., to miss, fail, err, sin
ἁμαρτάνω.s: ἁμαρτάνω, originally, I miss the mark; hence, (a) I make a mistake; (b) I sin, I commit a sin (against God); sometimes (Lk. xvii 4, Ac. xxv 8, &c.) the idea of sinning against a fellow-creature is present.

ἅπας.s: ἅπας, all, whole (cf. πᾶς). It is rather a literary word and is used by preference after consonants.

γενεά.s: γενεά, a generation: in combination with another γενεά, or with αἰών, practically indicates infinity of time.

δεύτερος.d: Deuteronomy, the second [statement of the] law
δεύτερος.s: δεύτερος, second: (τὸ) δεύτερον is used adverbially, in the second place, for the second time.

δέω.d: diadem, literally, something bound around or across
δέω.mg: to bind. Do not confuse w.

διώκω.s: διώκω, I pursue; hence, I persecute.

ἐπιγνώσκω.s: ἐπιγινώσκω, I come to know by directing my attention to (ἐπί) him or it, I perceive, discern, recognize: aor. I found out.

εὐλογέω.s: εὐλογέω, (lit. I speak well of, opp. I abuse, curse) I bless; εὐλογημένος, of a man, blessed (by God; contrast εὐλογητός): εὐλογῶν (or ἐν εὐλογίᾳ) εὐλογῶ (Hebraistic), I bless abundantly.

θαυμάζω.d: cf. thaumaturge, a worker of miracles or wonders
θαυμάζω.mg: to wonder, be amazed at, admire
θαυμάζω.s: θαυμάζω, (a) intr. I wonder; cognate acc. θαυμάζειν θαῦμα μέγα, Rev. xvii 6, to wonder very greatly; (b) tr. I wonder at, admire.

θεραπεύω.s: θεραπεύω, I care for, attend, serve, treat, especially of a physician; hence I heal, sometimes with ἀπό, of.

θηρίον.d: theriomorphic, having animal form; as, theriomorphic gods
θηρίον.s: θηρίον, properly a wild beast, hence any animal.

κατοικέω.s: κατοικέω, I dwell in (implying a more permanent settlement than παροικέω), I settle in, I am established in (permanently).

λύω.d: cf. analysis, a resolving or unloosing into simple elements
λύω.s: λύω (soluo), (a) I unloose, loose, loosen, untie, release, Mk. i 7, &c.: thus I break (in a phrase where the time order of the two processes is inverted), Rev. v 2; (b) met. I break, destroy, set at naught, contravene; sometimes merely, I declare a law to be not binding, John v 18; I break up a meeting, Ac. xiii 43; I annul, 1 John iv 3 (v.l.).

μέρος.d: in biology, pentamerous, of five parts
μέρος.s: μέρος, a part, portion: τὰ μέρη, territorially, the region; adv. phrases are ἀπὸ μέρους, ἐκ μέρους, in part, partly, ἀνὰ μέρος, κατὰ μέρος, part by part, each part separately, in detail; a party, Ac. xxiii 9.

ναός.s: ναός, a temple, a shrine, that part of the temple where the god himself resides (contrast ἱερόν); so also figuratively.

ὅμοιος.d: Homoiousian, one holding that Father and Son in the Godhead are of like [but not the same] substance; a Semi-Arian

σήμερον.s: σήμερον (hodie), adv. to-day, this day: ἡ σήμερον (sc. ἡμέρα, cf. hodiernus dies), noun, to-day, this day.

σπέρμα.s: σπέρμα (semen), (a) seed, commonly of cereals; (b) offspring, descendants, in the animal kingdom (frequent in Hebrew).

σταυρόω.s: σταυρόω, I crucify: hence met. Gal. vi 14.

συνίημι.s: συνίημι, I understand; I have understanding.

τιμή.s: τιμή, (a) honour, e.g. John iv 44; (b) price, e.g. Mt. xxvii 6.

φωνέω.s: φωνέω, I give forth a sound, hence: (a) of a cock, I crow; (b) of men, I shout; (c) tr. I call (to myself), I summon; I invite, Lk. xiv 12; I address, John xiii 13.

ἅπτομαι.mg: to fasten, kindle; mid., adhere to, take hold of, engage in
ἅπτομαι.s: ἅπτω, (a) act. I light, kindle; (b) mid. c. gen. I lay hold of, I cling to (eagerly).

ἄξιος.d: axiom; in philosophy and psychology, axiological, pertaining to the science of values

διέρχομαι.s: διέρχομαι, I go (come, journey) all the way through: in Ac. seems frequently to imply, I itinerate, evangelize as I go.

δικαιόω.s: δικαιόω, I make δίκαιος (righteous), I defend the cause of, plead for the righteousness (innocence) of, I acquit, justify; hence, I regard as δίκαιος (righteous).

ἐπιθυμία.s: ἐπιθυμία, eager (passionate) desire, passion: see ἐπιθυμέω.

ἐπιτίθημι.mg: to lay upon, impose, inflict; mid., attack
ἐπιτίθημι.s: ἐπιτίθημι, I place upon, lay on: with ὄνομα, I add, give in addition.

ἐργάζομαι.s: ἐργάζομαι, (a) I am at work, I work; (b) tr. I produce by work, put in force, give operation to, realize, e.g. Mt. vii 23; c. cogn. acc. ἔργον, ἔργα, Mt. xxvi 10, &c.; c. acc. βρῶσιν, I work for, John vi 27.

εὐχαριστέω.s: εὐχαριστέω, I give thanks: pass. 3 sing. is received with thanks, 2 Cor. i 11.

θύρα.s: θύρα, (a) a door; (b) met. an opportunity, Ac. xiv 27, 1 Cor. xvi 9, &c.

ἱκανός.s: ἱκανός, (a) considerable, sufficient, of number, quantity, time: ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων (v. l. ἱκανοῦ), already for a long time, Lk. xxiii 8 (cf. viii 27), ἐφ’ ἱκανόν, for a sufficiently long time, Ac. xx 11; ἱκανόν ἐστιν, enough of this subject, Lk. xxii 38 (cf. 2 Cor. ii 6); τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιεῖν τινι (satis facere alicui), to satisfy one, to give him no ground of complaint, Mk. xv 15, τὸ ἱκανὸν λαμβάνω (satis accipio), I get surety (security), Ac. xvii 9; (b) of persons, sufficiently strong (good, &c.), worthy, suitable, with various constructions.

κλαίω.s: κλαίω, I weep; c. acc. or ἐπί c. acc. I weep for, mourn.

λογίζομαι.s: λογίζομαι (properly of an accountant, book-keeper, I count, reckon up), (a) I reckon, count, put down to one’s account, τι or τινί τι, Rom. iv 6, 1 Cor. xiii 5, 2 Cor. v 19, 2 Tim. iv 16; also with εἴς τι = as something, as of some value, e.g. Ac. xix 27, Rom. iv 3, Gal. iii 6; (b) I number, class amongst, [Mk.] xv 28, Lk. xxii 37; (c) I reckon up accounts, I weigh arguments, I deliberate, Mk. xi 31 (v.l.); (d) hence I consider, weigh, John xi 50, 2 Cor. x 11, Phil. iv 8, Heb. xi 19; (e) I think, I judge, often; (f) I decide, determine, 2 Cor. x 2.

οἰκοδομέω.s: οἰκοδομέω, I build (a house); hence met.

ὀλίγος.s: ὀλίγος (ὁλίγος), (a) especially in the plural, few; (b) in the singular, small; hence, of time, short, of degree, light, slight, little: πρὸς ὀλίγον, to a slight degree, 1 Tim. iv 8, for a short time, James iv 14; ἐν ὀλίγῳ, in brief compass, in brief, in few words, briefly (cf. 1 Pet. v 12), Eph. iii 3, Ac. xxvi 28 (perhaps = in very short time); ὀλίγον (acc. neut.), adverbially, of space, a little, Mk. i 19, Lk. v 3, of time, for a short (little) time, Mk. vi 31, 1 Pet. i 6 (but more probably, to a little amount), v 10, Rev. xvii 10.

οὐαί.s: οὐαί (uae), adv., woe, c. dat. or acc., sometimes in Rev. made a noun ἡ οὐαί (=? ἡ κραυγὴ οὐαί); expresses rather a statement than a wish or imprecation, distress comes (will come) upon.

παραγίνομαι.s: παραγίνομαι, (a) I come on the scene, I appear, I come; (b) with words expressing destination, I present myself at, I arrive at, I reach.

παρίστημι.s: παριστάνω, παρίστημι, (a) in the transitive tenses, I cause to come to and stand beside; I bring; I present, offer, commend; I introduce (one person to another); I prove by argument, Ac. xxiv 13; (b) in the intransitive tenses, I come up to and stand by, sometimes with the idea of thus providing support (cf. 2 Tim. iv 17).

πάσχω.s: πάσχω, I am acted upon in a certain way, I experience certain treatment, e.g. Mt. xvii 15 (v. l.): hence (by a development from the original use), I experience ill treatment, &c., I suffer, e.g. Mt. xvii 12.

περισσεύω.s: περισσεύω, (a) intr. I exceed the ordinary (the necessary), I abound, I overflow; I am left over; hence met.: (b) tr. I cause to abound, Mt. xiii 12, Lk. xv 17, 2 Cor. iv 15 (?), ix 8, Eph. i 8, 1 Thess. iii 12.

πλανάω.d: planet, to the ancients, an apparently ‘wandering’ celestial body
πλανάω.s: πλανάω, (a) I cause to wander: hence, in the moral sense, I cause to err; (b) pass. I wander; hence I err.

πράσσω.d: praxis, practice, as opposed to theory
πράσσω.mg: to do, accomplish; εὖ or καλῶς πράττω, I fare well
πράσσω.s: πράσσω (ago, referring rather to the purpose, motive of an action than to the actual doing), (a) tr. I act, do; (b) tr. I exact, extort, Lk. iii 13, xix 23; (c) intr. I fare: εὖ πράξετε, you shall fare well, Ac. xv 29, τί πράσσω, how I fare, Eph. vi 21.

τέλος.d: teleology, in philosophy, the view that developments are due to the purpose or design [end] that is served by them
τέλος.s: τέλος, (a) sing. (τέλος dicitur Graece quod nos Latine et finem dicimus et consummationem; τέλος autem et consummationis ipsius finis est, Ambros. expos. ps. cxviii 12 45 § 1) the end, the final end of anything; εἰς τέλος, continually, Lk. xviii 5; the result, the culmination, e.g. 1 Pet. i 9; fulfilment, Lk. xxii 37; (b) especially plur. revenues, dues, Mt. xvii 25, also sing. Rom. xiii 7: of the spiritual revenues of the ages, 1 Cor. x 11.

χωρίς.g: with the gen., without, apart from
χωρίς.mg: separately; prep. with gen., apart, beside
χωρίς.s: χωρίς, apart from, separately from; without.

ἀγρός.s: ἀγρός (a word rare in papyrus documents, and now obsolete), a field, especially as bearing a crop; the country, Mk. xv 21, xvi 12: plur. ἀγροί, lands, property in land, a country estate.

ἄρτι.s: ἄρτι (of present time), now, just now.

ἄρχων.s: ἄρχων, a ruler, governor, leader, leading man; with the Jews, an official member (a member of the executive) of the γερουσία.

ἀσθενέω.s: ἀσθενέω, I am weak (physically: then morally), I am sick.

βλασφημέω.s: βλασφημέω, I speak evil against, I use abusive or scurrilous language about (God or men).

διάβολος.g: slanderous, accusing falsly; as a noun, the Accuser, the Devil
διάβολος.s: διάβολος (adj. used oftener as noun), slanderous (1 Tim. iii 11, 2 Tim. iii 3, Tit. ii 3); almost always ὁ Διάβολος, the Slanderer (par excellence), the Devil.

διακονέω.g: I wait upon (especially at table), serve (generally), minister
διακονέω.s: διακονέω (ministro), I wait at table (particularly of a slave who pours out wine to the guests); I serve (generally).

ἐκπορεύομαι.s: ἐκπορεύομαι, I journey out; I come forth.

ἐπιστρέφω.s: ἐπιστρέφω, (a) tr. I turn (back) to (towards); (b) intr. I turn (back) (to [towards]); I come to myself, Lk. xxii 32.

καλῶς.s: καλῶς, well, nobly, honourably; in a good place, James ii 3: compar. κάλλιον; καλῶς ποιήσεις, especially with aor. participle, is idiomatic for please, 3 John 6, cf. Ac. x 33, Phil. iv 14, 2 Pet. i 19.

μάρτυς.s: μάρτυς, a witness, eye- or ear-witness. In Ac. xxii 20, Rev. ii 13 it approaches the ecclesiastical sense of martyr, i.e. one who gives public testimony to his faith before a tribunal, and suffers the penalty.

μετανοέω.s: μετανοέω, I change my mind, I change the inner man (particularly with reference to acceptance of the will of God by the νοῦς (mind) instead of rejection): with ἀπό or ἐκ, the giving up definitely of the courses denoted by the following words is indicated.

ὀπίσω.g: behind, after; with the gen., behind, after
ὀπίσω.d: cf. opisthograph, a manuscript written upon both the back and the front, Rev. 5:1
ὀπίσω.s: ὀπίσω, adv. and prep., behind; after: εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω (Mk. xiii 16) = ὀπίσω (Mt. xxiv 18), cf. Lk. ix 62.

ὀργή.s: ὀργή, anger, wrath, passion; the settled feeling of anger (cf. Eph. iv 31), particularly, τοῦ θεοῦ, of God, the hostility to sin: ἡ μέλλουσα (ἐρχομένη) ὀργή also refers to the divine wrath, and has a definite eschatological reference; occasionally also without epithet, of the divine wrath, e.g. Rom. iii 5, v 9, ix 22, xiii 5, 1 Thess. ii 16.

ὀφείλω.s: ὀφείλω (debeo), I owe: c. infin. I ought.

πειράζω.s: πειράζω, (a) I make trial of, try, test, explore; God tests man by means of suffering or in some other way, man tests God by seeking how far it is possible to go on disobeying Him, without provoking his anger; (b) a secondary neutral or evil sense, I tempt, Mt. iv 1, Mk. i 13, Lk. iv 2, 1 Cor. vii 5, James i 13 (second occurrence), 14: if trial fails, the result is moral evil: the agency of Satan is interposed, the same process being carried on for God’s good purpose and his evil purpose; thus ὁ πειράζων comes to indicate the intermediary, the Tempter, Mt. iv 3, 1 Thess. iii 5; (c) c. inf. I try, attempt.

περιτομή.s: περιτομή (circumcisio), circumcision (see περιτέμνω); οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς, the party of circumcision, the party advocating circumcision, the rigorist Christian Jews: sometimes met. (as in O.T.), of that chastening of the heart (mind) which leads to heartier service to God, e.g. Rom. ii 29.

προσευχή.s: προσευχή, (a) prayer (to God); τοῦ θεοῦ, to God, Lk. vi 12; (b) a place for prayer, Ac. xvi 13 (used by Jews, perhaps where there was no synagogue).

πτωχός.g: poor; as a noun, a poor man
πτωχός.s: πτωχός (strictly a beggar; weakened afterwards), poor; a poor man: met. (Mt. v 3, Lk. vi 20, Rev. iii 17), not of those who are poor in material things, but of the humble devout persons, who feel the need of God’s help.

τέσσαρες.d: the Diatessaron of Tatian, a harmony of the four Gospels made about A.D. 170; literally, through [the] four

ὑποστρέφω.s: ὑποστρέφω, intr. I return; I withdraw, met., 2 Pet. ii 21.

ὑποτάσσω.d: in grammar, hypotaxis, subordination of clauses
ὑποτάσσω.s: ὑποτάσσω (lit. I put in a lower rank, I rank under, a military term), I subject, I put into subjection: mid. (and pass.) I subordinate myself, I put myself into subjection, I submit.

ἀναγινώσκω.s: ἀναγινώσκω, I read aloud (in the scriptures, i.e. the Old Testament).

ἀρνέομαι.s: ἀρνέομαι, (a) I deny (a statement); (b) I repudiate (a person, or belief).

βιβλίον.s: βιβλίον (libellus, originally a diminutive), a papyrus roll: ἀποστασίου, document of divorce, handed by the husband to the wife whom he divorces: ζωῆς, of life, preserved in heaven and containing the names of those who share in [eternal] life.

δεικνύω or δείκνυμι.d: in logic, apodeictic, of clear demonstration
δεικνύω or δείκνυμι.s: δείκνυμι, δεικνύω, I point out, show.

διαθήκη.s: διαθήκη, (a) = συνθήκη, a covenant between two parties; (b) (the ordinary, everyday sense [found a countless number of times in papyri]) a will, testament, Gal. iii 15, 17, Heb. ix 16. See my Text and Canon, p. 157, n. 2.

διακονία.g: waiting at table, (in a wider sense) service, ministry
διακονία.s: διακονία (ministerium), waiting at table; in a wider sense, service, ministration.

δυνατός.s: δυνατός, (a) of persons, powerful, able; (b) of things, possible.

ἔξεστι.s: ἔξεστιν, impers. it is permitted (allowed), sometimes followed by acc. et inf.: ἐξόν ἐστιν = ἔξεστιν, the ἔστιν being understood in Ac. ii 29, 2 Cor. xii 4.

ἐχθρός.g: hating; as a noun, an enemy
ἐχθρός.mg: hated, hateful, hostile; ὁ ἐχθρός, enemy

ἥλιος.s: ἥλιος, the sun; μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον, equivalent to stone-blind, Ac. xiii 11.

ἱερεύς.s: ἱερεύς, a priest, one who offers sacrifice to a god (in Jewish and pagan religions; of Christians only metaphorically).

καυχάομαι.s: καυχάομαι, I boast; I glory (exult) proudly.

μέλος.s: μέλος (membrum, but wider in sense than κῶλον), a bodily organ, limb, member.

μήτε.mg: and not, nor; μήτε... μήτε, neither... nor
μήτε.s: μήτε (= μή τε), nor: μήτε... μήτε, neither... nor, sometimes also oftener than twice (e.g. James v 12).

οἶνος.s: οἶνος, wine; met. Rev. (except vi 6, xviii 13), where almost otiose.

πλῆθος.s: πλῆθος, a multitude, a crowd, a large number

ποῖος.s: ποῖος (qualis), properly direct interrogative, of what sort?, then often weakened to what? simply: also indir. interrog.: ποίας (local genitive, sc. ὁδοῦ), by what way.

συνέρχομαι.s: συνέρχομαι, I go along with, I accompany; I come (meet) together with others, αὐτῷ in Mk. xiv 53 being = πρὸς αὐτόν: (conuenio) I have sexual intercourse, Mt. i 18.

ὑπομονή.s: ὑπομονή, stedfast endurance, the virtue shown by martyrs.

φυλάσσω.mg: to guard; mid., be on one’s guard, take care
φυλάσσω.s: φυλάσσω, (a) I guard, protect, with personal or other concrete object, or (Lk. ii 8) cognate acc.; mid. I am on my guard, Lk. xii 15; (b) act. and mid., of customs or regulations, I keep, I observe.

ἀκάθαρτος.s: ἀκάθαρτος, unclean, impure: in reference to demons, spirits, Mt. x 1, &c.

ἄνεμος.s: ἄνεμος, wind (literally, and in Eph. iv 14 metaph.): in the sense quarter of the heaven, cardinal point, as both Greeks and Romans habitually defined the quarters of the heaven by the winds which came from those quarters, Mt. xxiv 31 (Mk. xiii 27).

ἀρνίον.s: ἀρνίον (originally, a little lamb, but diminutive force was lost), a lamb: see ἀρήν.

γε.mg: particle, indeed, truly, at least, yet
γε.s: γε, an enclitic, emphasizing particle (quidem), at least, indeed, really, but generally too subtle to be represented in English.

διάκονος.s: διάκονος (minister), a waiter, servant: then of any one who performs any service, an administrator, &c.

ἐλπίζω.mg: to hope for or that, expect
ἐλπίζω.s: ἐλπίζω (ἑλπίζω), I hope, hope for: the substantive following ἐν, εἰς, ἐπί with dat. or acc., is the ground of the hope, that which makes hope possible.

ἐπικαλέω.g: I call, name; middle, I invoke, appeal to
ἐπικαλέω.s: ἐπικαλέω, (a) I call (name) by a supplementary (additional, alternative) name; (b) mid. I call upon, appeal to, address.

ἐπιτιμάω.s: ἐπιτιμάω, (a) I rebuke, chide, censure; (b) c. ἵνα, I warn.

καθαρίζω.s: καθαρίζω (alternative spelling καθερίζω, perhaps = καθαιρίζω, but it occurs only in augmented and reduplicated forms and has been otherwise explained) (purgo), I make clean, literally, ceremonially, or spiritually, according to context, ἀπό c. gen. being sometimes added, of the dirt removed.

ναί.s: ναί, yes, sometimes made a substantive by prefixing the article τό.

ὁμοίως.s: ὁμοίως, in a similar way, similarly, in the same way.

παραγγέλλω.s: παραγγέλλω, I command, I charge; παραγγελίᾳ παραγγέλλειν (Hebraism), to charge strictly, Ac. v 28.

παρέρχομαι.g: I pass by, pass away; I arrive
παρέρχομαι.s: παρέρχομαι, tr. and intr. I pass by, I pass: sometimes practically, I pass out of sight, I disappear: c. acc. (cf. παραβαίνω) I transgress: intr. I approach, come up to, Lk. xii 37, xvii 7, [Ac.] xxiv 7.

παρρησία.s: παρρησία, boldness, freedom, liberty, shown especially in speech; ἐν παρρησίᾳ, μετὰ παρρησίας, quite openly (opposite to ‘secretly’).

πλήν.g: however, but, only; with the gen., except
πλήν.s: πλήν, (a) conjunction, (1) however, nevertheless, Mt. xxvi 39 (Lk. xxii 42), Mt. xi 22, 24, xxvi 64, &c.; (2) but, Lk. xii 31, xxiii 28; (3) πλὴν ὅτι, except that, save that, Ac. xx 23; (4) only, in any case, ending the discussion and calling special attention to the essential, especially in Paul, e.g. 1 Cor. xi 11, Eph. v 33; (b) preposition, except, apart from.

σκανδαλίζω.s: σκανδαλίζω (a Hebraistic, Biblical word), I put a stumbling-block in the way of, I cause to stumble, I set a trap for (in the moral sphere).

σκότος.d: scotoscope, a fieldglass for seeing by night
σκότος.s: σκότος, darkness: frequent in the conceptions of Jewish eschatology, Mt. viii 12, xxii 13, xxv 30: met. of the darkness of ignorance and sin, Lk. i 79, John iii 19, &c.

συνείδησις.s: συνείδησις, (originally consciousness, e.g. 1 Pet. ii 19, where θεοῦ is objective genitive, but through the influence of the Stoic terminology) conscience, the innate power to discern what is good, an abiding consciousness bearing witness concerning a man’s conduct.

φαίνω.s: φαίνω, (a) act. I shine, I shed light; (b) pass. (1) I shine; (2) I become visible, I appear, cf. ἐφάνη, impersonally, Mt. ix 33; (3) I become clear, appear, show myself as, Mt. vi 5, 16, 18, xxiii 27, Rom. vii 13, 2 Cor. xiii 7, 1 Pet. iv 18; (4) of the mind and judgement (= δοκεῖ, uidetur), Mk. xiv 64, Lk. xxiv 11.

φεύγω.mg: to flee, be prosecuted, be banished

φυλή.d: in zoology, phylum, one of the large fundamental divisions of the animal kingdom
φυλή.s: φυλή, a tribe, especially one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and perhaps (by analogy) of Christendom, James i 1.

ἀληθινός.s: ἀληθινός (less common than ἀληθής), true (lit. made of truth), real, genuine.

γαμέω.d: in biology, gamete, a matured germ cell
γαμέω.s: γαμέω, I marry, used of either sex.

ἐνδύω.s: ἐνδύω, I put on, clothe (another): mid. I clothe (myself), dress: hence, metaphorically, of acquiring qualities; = ἐπενδύομαι, 2 Cor. v 3.

ἐπεί.s: ἐπεί, (a) after, Lk. vii 1 (v. l.), Ac. xiii 46 (v.l.); (b) for, since; (c) otherwise, Rom. xi 6. 22, 1 Cor. v 10, &c.

ἡγέομαι.g: I am chief; I think, regard
ἡγέομαι.s: ἡγέομαι, (a) I lead: ὁ ἡγούμενος (as subst.), the leader; (b) (cf. duco) I think, I am of opinion.

θυσία.s: θυσία, abstr. and concr., sacrifice; a sacrifice.

ἰσχυρός.s: ἰσχυρός, strong (originally and generally of physical strength); powerful.

κρίμα.s: κρίμα, (a) a judgement, a verdict; sometimes implying an adverse verdict, a condemnation; (b) a case at law, a lawsuit, 1 Cor. vi 7.

μάχαιρα.s: μάχαιρα, a sword: met. of the spirit, Eph. vi 17.

μισθός.s: μισθός (merces), (a) pay, wages, salary; (b) reward, recompense.

μυστήριον.s: μυστήριον, a secret, Mk. iv 11 and parallels: also (a) a symbol containing a secret meaning, Rev. xvii 5, cf. Eph. v 32; (b) the meaning of such a symbol, Rev. i 20, xvii 7; (c) as the counterpart of ἀποκάλυψις, a secret to be revealed, the secret purpose of God in His dealings with man, a Divine secret, especially the inclusion of the Gentiles as well as the Jews in the scope of the Messiah’s beneficent reign; (d) the sum of the Christian faith, 1 Tim. iii 9, 16.

παράκλησις.d: cf. Paraclete, the Comforter, Helper, Advocate, or Counselor
παράκλησις.s: παράκλησις, an appeal, which according to circumstances may be either hortatory, exhortation, or consolatory, consolation: in Lk. ii 25 it seems to have a quasi-technical sense, with reference to the coming of the Messiah.

πάσχα.s: πάσχα (Hebrew, Aramaic), the feast of passover, the paschal meal, which took place on the night of full moon after the spring equinox, that is the night between 14th and 15th Nisan. On the afternoon of 14th Nisan before sunset the paschal lamb, also called τὸ πάσχα (so met., 1 Cor. v 7), was sacrificed.

πλούσιος.mg: rich. ὁ πλούσιος, a rich man
πλούσιος.s: πλούσιος, rich, wealthy: hence, met., of other than material wealth.

πόθεν.s: πόθεν (unde), whence? from what place? also indirect interrogative: hence how? e.g. Mk. xii 37, John i 48.

ποτέ.s: ποτέ, indefinite temporal particle, at any time, ever, at some time; at one time, especially with past tenses: for μή ποτε, see μήποτε.

προφητεύω.s: προφητεύω, I do the duty of a προφήτης, I declare the will of God, sometimes with regard to what is to happen in the future, in which case it may be rendered, I prophesy.

τελέω.d: cf. teleology, in philosophy, the view that developments are due to the purpose or design [τέλος] that is served by them
τελέω.s: τελέω, (a) I end, complete, accomplish, finish: also I fulfil; in Gal. v 16, possibly I perform; (b) of taxes, dues, I pay, Mt. xvii 24, Rom. xiii 6.

φίλος.g: loving; as a noun, a friend

ἁγιάζω.d: cf. hagiolatry, the worship of saints
ἁγιάζω.s: ἁγιάζω (apparently exclusively Biblical), I make ἅγιος, treat as ἅγιος (set apart, holy), sanctify, hallow (see ἅγιος).

ἀδελφή.s: ἀδελφή, (a) a sister; (b) a woman (fellow-)member of a church, a Christian woman (Rom. xvi 1; 1 Cor. vii 15, &c.).

ἀδικία.s: ἀδικία, injustice, unrighteousness, hurt; sometimes in a Hebraistic genitive, equivalent to the adjective ἄδικος (e.g. Lk. xvi 8, xviii 6).

ἀληθής.s: ἀληθής, true in fact; hence more widely (see ἀλήθεια).

ἀποκαλύπτω.s: ἀποκαλύπτω, I unveil, reveal (correlative to μυστήριον, secret).

βαστάζω.s: βαστάζω, (a) I carry, bear; (b) I carry (take) away, Mt. iii 11, John xx 15; I pilfer, John xii 6.

ἑορτή.s: ἑορτή, a festival, feast, periodically recurring: ποιεῖν ἑορτήν, Ac. xviii 21 = ἑορτάζειν.

ἥκω.s: ἥκω, I have come, but other tenses are translated as if the present meant I come.

θυγάτηρ.s: θυγάτηρ, a daughter; hence (Hebraistic?), of any female descendant, however far removed, Lk. i 5, xiii 16; even of one unrelated, my young lady, Mk. v 34, &c.

ἰάομαι.d: cf. pediatrics, medical care of children [παῖς, παιδός]
ἰάομαι.s: ἰάομαι, I heal, generally of physical, sometimes of spiritual, disease.

καταργέω.s: καταργέω, (a) I make idle (inactive), I make of no effect, I annul, abolish, bring to naught; (b) with ἀπό, I discharge, sever, separate from.

λυπέω.mg: to annoy; pass. and fut. mid., be grieved, distressed

νικάω.d: cf. Nicholas, victor over the people [λαός]
νικάω.s: νικάω, I conquer (transferred from battle to other conflicts).

ὀμνύω or ὄμνυμι.s: ὄμνυμι, ὀμνύω, I swear, I take an oath: sometimes with cognate acc. or with dat.: with acc., or with κατά c. gen., of the power invoked or appealed to, by, James v 12, Heb. vi 13, 16.

πόσος.s: πόσος (quantus), how great?, how large?: in plur. (quot, later quanti), how many?: πόσῳ (quanto), before compar. (cf. Mt. xii 12), by how much?, how much?

σταυρός.s: σταυρός, a cross (crux), strictly the transverse beam (patibulum), which was placed at the top of the vertical part, thus forming a capital T. It was this transverse beam that was carried by the criminal: the crucifixion of Jesus.

στρατιώτης.s: στρατιώτης, a soldier: hence (perhaps under the influence of the language of the Mysteries and that of philosophy), the worshipper as the soldier of his God, cf. 2 Tim. ii 3.

φρονέω.s: φρονέω, c. acc. I have in my mind, I think of, I set my mind upon, suggesting my moral interest, thought, and study, and not a mere unreflecting opinion: intr. I think, I cherish a habit of thought.

χώρα.d: chorography, describing, or description, of districts
χώρα.s: χώρα (regio, an official term), strictly used, a region, a great geographical (and sometimes administrative) division of a province, e.g. Ac. xvi 6, xviii 23, but often more loosely, country, district: hence met., e.g. Mt. iv 16; sometimes almost a field, John iv 35, James v 4.

ἀδικέω.mg: to do wrong, injure; pass. be wronged
ἀδικέω.s: ἀδικέω, I act unjustly towards, I injure, I harm (animate or inanimate).

ἀναβλέπω.s: ἀναβλέπω, (a) I look up, e.g. Mt. xiv 19; (b) I recover my sight, e.g. Mt. xi 5.

δέκα.d: Decapolis, the region embracing ten cities mostly SE. of the Lake of Tiberias

δουλεύω.s: δουλεύω, I serve as a slave, I am a slave.

ἕνεκα or ἕνεκεν.g: with the gen., on account of
ἕνεκα or ἕνεκεν.mg: on account of, for the sake of, as far as regards
ἕνεκα or ἕνεκεν.s: ἕνεκα, ἕνεκεν, εἵνεκεν, for the sake of, on account of: οὗ (neut.) εἵνεκεν, on account of which, wherefore, Lk. iv 18; τίνος ἕνεκα, on account of what, wherefore, why, Ac. xix 32.

καθαρός.s: καθαρός (purus), clean, pure, unstained, either literally or ceremonially or spiritually; καθαρὸς ἀπό, unstained by.

μανθάνω.s: μανθάνω, I learn; with adjectives or nouns, I learn to be so and so, 1 Tim. v 13; with acc. of person who is the object of knowledge, Eph. iv 20; aor. sometimes to ascertain, Ac. xxiii 27, Gal. iii 2.

μήποτε.s: μήποτε (= μή ποτε), lest at any time, lest: then weakened, whether perhaps, whether at all; in a principal clause, perhaps.

ὁμολογέω.s: ὁμολογέω (originally, I agree with the statement of another), (a) I promise, Mt. xiv 7, Ac. vii 17; (b) I confess (confiteor); (c) I publicly declare (profiteor), cf. 1 John ii 23, iv 3, sometimes with the Aramaic and Syriac construction, ἐν c. dat. equivalent to an acc., Mt. x 32, Lk. xii 8, of confessing allegiance to Jesus before an earthly law-court: c. cognate acc. 1 Tim. vi 12; (d) a Hebraism, I praise, celebrate, Heb. xiii 15 (cf. ἐξομολογέομαι).

οὗ.mg: 3 pers. (reflex. in Attic), of him, her, it
οὗ.s: οὗ, relative adverb, where; also whither.

πνευματικός.s: πνευματικός, having the characteristics of πνεῦμα, spiritual, with general reference to the higher nature of man as directly in touch with and influenced by the divine, but sometimes (like πνεῦμα) associated with the demonic world, τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας, the spiritual hosts of evil, Eph. vi 12: supernatural, 1 Cor. x 3.

πορνεία.s: πορνεία, fornication, the practice of consorting with πόρναι or πόρνοι, habitual immorality.

προσέχω.g: I attend to, give heed to
προσέχω.s: προσέχω, (a) (τὸν νοῦν was originally added, I direct the mind), I attend to, pay attention to, c. dat., Ac. viii 6, xvi 14, &c. cf. (c); (b) with ἐμαυτῷ, or absolutely, I attend to myself, I pay attention for myself, Hebraistic for I am cautious, I beware, I take care for (of) myself, Lk. xvii 3, Ac. v 35, with ἀπό governing the thing of which one has to beware, Mt. vii 15, Lk. xii 1, &c.; so with μή, lest; (c) sc. ἐμαυτόν, I attach myself to, I join, Ac. viii 10, 1 Tim. iv 1; I devote myself to (by way of enjoyment or of work), 1 Tim. i 4, iii 8, iv 13, Tit. i 14, Heb. vii 13.

φιλέω.s: φιλέω, I love, of friendship (contrast ἔραμαι [of passion] and ἀγαπάω [of reverential love]): I kiss, Mk. xiv 44, Mt. xxvi 48, Lk. xxii 47.

ἀκοή.s: ἀκοή, (a) hearing, faculty of hearing; ear: in ἀκοῇ ἀκούειν (Mt. xiii 14, &c.), a Hebraistic (?) expression, the ἀκοῇ is emphatic; (b) report, rumour.

ἀναιρέω.mg: to take up, destroy; mid. take up one's own
ἀναιρέω.s: ἀναιρέω, (a) I take up, e.g. Ac. vii 21; more often (b) I take away the life of, murder (2 Thess. ii 8, text doubtful).

ἀσθένεια.s: ἀσθένεια, want of strength, weakness, illness.

ἀσθενής.s: ἀσθενής (lit. not strong), (a) weak (physically, or morally); (b) ill.

διότι.mg: conj. for διὰ τοῦτο ὅτι..., because that, for the reason that
διότι.s: διότι (= διὰ ὅ τι), wherefore; = ὅτι Rom. viii 21 (v.l.).

ἐκλεκτός.s: ἐκλεκτός, chosen out, selected, sometimes as substantive, of those chosen out by God for the rendering of special service to Him (of the Hebrew race, particular Hebrews, the Messiah, and the Christians): an adj. in 2 John 1, 13.

καταλείπω.s: καταλείπω, I leave behind; I desert, abandon.

κατηγορέω.s: κατηγορέω (accuso), I accuse, charge; I prosecute.

κεῖμαι.mg: to lie, lie down, repose, be situated
κεῖμαι.s: κεῖμαι, a perf. used instead of the perf. pass. of τίθημι, I have been placed (put, laid), hence, I lie: the former sense explains the construction with εἰς and acc.

νοῦς.s: νοῦς (a non-Semitic Greek term, meaning in Plato reason, intuition, sometimes in the LXX taking the place of the commoner καρδία as a rendering of Hebrew lēb), the intellectual faculty of the natural man, applicable to God or Christ (Rom. xi 34, 1 Cor. ii 16), employed in practical judgement, capable of being good or evil, and of being regenerated, the mind, the reason, the reasoning faculty.

παῖς.s: παῖς, (a) a male child, a boy; (b) (cf. παιδίον) a male slave, a servant; thus a servant of God, especially as a title of the Messiah (from Isa. xli–liii) Ac. iv 27, 30; (c) a female child, a girl, Lk. viii 51, 54.

πάρειμι.g: I am present; I have arrived
πάρειμι.mg: to be present. π. εἰς τὰ βασίλεια, to be present in; lit., to have come (arrived) into. πάρεστι, it is permitted or possible
πάρειμι.s: πάρειμι, I am present; I have come, arrived (hence with εἰς, πρός).

παρουσία.g: presence, coming (especially Christ's [second] coming in glory)
παρουσία.s: παρουσία (in ordinary Greek = presence; arrival; also, technical term with reference to the visit of a king or some other official, a royal visit), (a) presence, as opposed to ‘absence’, 1 Cor. xvi 17, 2 Cor. vii 6, 7 (cf. x 10), Phil. i 26, ii 12; (b) a technical eschatological term, representing a word used by Jesus Himself, the presence, coming, arrival, advent of the glorified Messiah, to be followed by a permanent residence with His people (so, in 2 Thess. ii 9, of that of the Lawless One).

περιβάλλω.s: περιβάλλω, I cast around, Lk. xix 43 (v.l.); I wrap a garment about, I put on: hence mid. I put on to myself, I clothe myself, I dress.

σωτήρ.s: σωτήρ (a word familiar to the Graeco-Roman world as a constant epithet of kings like the Ptolemies and of the Roman emperors, especially in the phrase ὁ σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου [cf. John iv 42, 1 John iv 14], connoting probably preserver from the enemies of the nation or the empire, and thus a maintainer of life and prosperity), saviour, rescuer, preserver, a term applied to (the) God and to the Messiah with respect to the human race and sin and its consequences.

ἀμπελών.s: ἀμπελών, a vineyard (-ών [=Lat. -etum] indicates ‘plantation of’, cf. ἐλαιών).

ἀνάγω.g: I lead up; middle, I put to sea, set sail
ἀνάγω.mg: to lead up, put to sea (usu. mid. or pass.)
ἀνάγω.s: ἀνάγω, (a) I lead up; (b) mid. and pass. I put to sea, set sail.

ἄπιστος.s: ἄπιστος, unbelieving, incredulous; unchristian: sometimes substantivally, unbeliever.

αὐξάνω.mg: to increase, honor; pass. grow, increase in size
αὐξάνω.s: αὐξάνω (αὔξω), (a) tr. (augeo) I cause to increase; (b) intr. (cresco) I increase, grow; with cogn. acc. Col. ii 19.

γρηγορέω.s: γρηγορέω (uigilo), (a) I am awake (in the night), watch; (b) I am watchful, on the alert.

ἐλευθερός.s: ἐλεύθερος, free (opposite of enslaved, cf. 1 Cor. xii 13).

κοπιάω.s: κοπιάω, (a) I grow weary, Mt. xi 28, John iv 6, Rev. ii 3; (b) I toil, work with effort (of bodily and mental labour alike).

κωλύω.s: κωλύω, I prevent, debar, hinder: c. infin. from doing so and so.

μιμνήσκομαι.s: μιμνήσκομαι, mid. and pass. (memoror), I remember: the passive forms sometimes have passive sense, from active μιμνήσκω (memoro), I call to mind, I recall, I mention, Ac. x 31, Rev. xvi 19.

νέος.s: νέος, (a) young; (b) new, fresh; Νέα πόλις, Neapolis, New City, the harbour town of Philippi.

πεινάω.s: πεινάω, I hunger, either lit. or met.: c. acc. I hunger for.

πέραν.s: πέραν (ultra), beyond, on the other side of, across; sometimes elliptically used, πέραν = (ἀπὸ) τῆς πέραν, Mk. iii 8 (Mt. iv 25), πέραν = τῆς πέραν, Mk. x 1: τὸ πέραν, as substantive, the other side, the country beyond.

περισσός.s: περισσός, over and above, excessive, abundant, overflowing; superfluous. Practically a synonym for πλείων (cf. Mt. v 37), especially in the comparative περισσότερος: ἐκ περισσοῦ, superabundantly, exceedingly.

σκεῦος.s: σκεῦος, (a) (uas) a vessel, generally of earthenware, e.g. John xix 29; τὰ σκεύη, utensils, goods and chattels, effects, property; (b) (Hebraistic) met. of persons, e.g. of St. Paul as chosen repository of the power of Jesus, Ac. ix 15: either of one’s own body as the case enclosing the soul, or of one’s wife, 1 Thess. iv 4 (cf. 1 Pet. iii 7); (c) tackle, furniture of a ship, Ac. xxvii 17.

τελειόω.s: τελειόω, I bring to completion, I complete: of persons, I bring to ethical or spiritual maturity (completeness): I fulfil, John xix 28.

χαρίζομαι.s: χαρίζομαι, (a) I graciously confer, Lk. vii 21, &c.; (b) I pardon, forgive, 2 Cor. ii 7, 10, xii 13, Eph. iv 32, Col. ii 13, iii 13; (c) I show kindness to, Gal. iii 18.

δοκιμάζω.s: δοκιμάζω, I put to the test, I prove, examine: in Rom. ii 18, Phil. i 10 either I distinguish by testing, or, more probably, I approve after testing: I think fit, Rom. i 28.

καθεύδω.s: καθεύδω, I am sleeping (asleep), I sleep.

καθίστημι.mg: to station, establish, appoint; in the intransitive tenses, take one’s place, be established, become, fall
καθίστημι.s: καθίστημι, καθιστάνω, in the tr. tenses (see ἵστημι), I set, establish, appoint, constitute, make; I conduct, Ac. xvii 15: καθίσταται, shows itself, acts its part, James iii 6.

κατεργάζομαι.s: κατεργάζομαι, I work out; I produce, accomplish.

κοιλία.g: the belly (stomach or intestines, or both), womb
κοιλία.s: κοιλία, belly, abdomen, a general term covering any organ in the abdomen, e.g. stomach, womb: ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός, from birth.

μετάνοια.s: μετάνοια, a change of mind, a change in the inner man: ἀπό indicates what is given up in this change, Heb. vi 1.

νυνί.s: νυνί (originally a more emphatic νῦν), now.

πληγή.s: πληγή, a blow, especially, caused by the lash, a stripe, a stroke.

πλοῦτος.s: πλοῦτος (masc. and neut.), wealth, material or spiritual.

πωλέω.s: πωλέω (originally = uendito, I advertise, put up for sale: later = uendo), I sell.

στρέφω.mg: to turn; mid. and pass., turn around
στρέφω.s: στρέφω, tr. I turn; hence, I bring back (?), Mt. xxvii 3; I change, Rev. xi 6; act. intr. Ac. vii 42: mid. and pass. intr. I turn, also met. I change.

συνέδριον.s: συνέδριον, a council of leading Jews, Mk. xiii 9, Mt. x 17, but elsewhere the Jewish council at Jerusalem, the Sanhedrin (Aramaic form of συνέδριον), the High Court, the Senate, composed of 71 members comprising members of high-priestly families, Pharisees learned in the law, and a lay element of Elders.

χιλίαρχος.s: χιλίαρχος (lit. a ruler of a thousand) (tribunus militum), a tribune, a Roman officer commanding a cohort, that is, about a thousand men), a colonel.

ὡσεί.s: ὡσεί, as if, as it were, like; with numbers, about.

ἀγνοέω.s: ἀγνοέω, I do not know, I am ignorant of (a person, thing, or fact), sometimes with the idea of wilful ignorance.

ἀντί.g: with the gen., instead of, for
ἀντί.mg: prep. w. gen. only, for, in return for, instead of
ἀντί.s: ἀντί (originally local, in front of, opposite), (a) instead of, in return for, in exchange for, as a substitute for; λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν Mk. x 45 (=Mt. xx 28), a ransom to buy the many, for the many; cf. Heb. xii 16 and ἀντίλυτρον; (b) ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ, on my behalf, Mt. xvii 27; (c) ἀνθ᾽ ὧν (literally, in return for which things) has become a conjunction, wherefore, because.

ἀργύριον.d: in pharmacy, Argyrol, the trade-name of a silver-protein compound
ἀργύριον.s: ἀργύριον, a piece of silver-money (except 1 Cor. iii 12, where silver).

βασιλεύω.s: βασιλεύω, (a) I rule, reign; (b) I reign over, c. gen.

ἑκατοντάρχης (or -αρχος).s: ἑκατοντάρχης (-ος) (centurio, see κεντουρίων), a centurion of the Roman army.

ἐκλέγομαι.s: ἐκλέγομαι, I pick out for myself, I choose.

εὐδοκέω.g: I think it good, am well pleased with
εὐδοκέω.s: εὐδοκέω, I am well-pleased, c. acc. expressing with, Mt. xii 18, &c.; I think it good, am resolved (a characteristic word of Jewish Greek).

ἐφίστημι.mg: to set over; mid., pass., 2 ao. and the perfects, stand upon
ἐφίστημι.s: ἐφίστημι: in intr. tenses and passive, I come upon (suddenly or unexpectedly) and stand by: met. I press forward, 2 Tim. iv 2.

λατρεύω.s: λατρεύω, I serve, especially God, perhaps simply I worship.

μνημονεύω.s: μνημονεύω, I remember; I hold in remembrance; I make mention of, Heb. xi 22.

παράπτωμα.s: παράπτωμα (delictum), a falling away, a lapse, a slip, a false step, a trespass.

πειρασμός.s: πειρασμός (from πειράζω, which see), (a) trial, probation, testing, being tried; (b) temptation, Mk. xiv 38 and parallels, Mt. vi 13, Lk. iv 13; (c) in Gal. iv 14 the reading τὸν πειρασμόν (without ὑμῶν or other addition) has been taken, on the analogy of modern popular Greek usage, = the devil, the demonic power as the cause of the Apostle’s infirmity.

τελώνης.s: τελώνης, collector (receiver) of customs, tax-gatherer, revenue official, of any rank, but especially of Jews of the lower rank, who collected revenue for the Roman overlord, detested by their fellow-countrymen and practically identified with ἁμαρτωλοί.

τεσσαράκοντα.s: τεσσαράκοντα (the spelling τεσσεράκοντα is late and illiterate), forty.

τιμάω.s: τιμάω, I honour, give honour to.

ὑπακούω.s: ὑπακούω, I obey: c. infin., Heb. xi 8.

χιλιάς.s: χιλιάς, a thousand, looked upon as a unit.

αἰτία.s: αἰτία, (a) a cause, reason; excuse; (b) a charge, accusation; (c) guilt; (d) relationship, matter, circumstances, case (= causa), Mt. xix 10.

ἀκροβυστία.s: ἀκροβυστία (a technical word of Jewish use, adapted from ἀκροποσθία [?]), foreskin, prepuce: used sometimes as a slang term by Jews, of Gentiles (Eph. ii 11).

βάπτισμα.s: βάπτισμα, a dipping, a baptism: c. gen. μετανοίας, belonging to a change of mental attitude, sign of a change of mental attitude.

ἐνεργέω.s: ἐνεργέω, (a) intr. I am at work, work; (b) tr. I work, the acc. expressing ‘that which is worked’, effect. In N.T. the word is generally connected with miraculous interpositions; (c) in the passive always with non-personal subject, as ἐνεργεῖν always with personal, I am made operative (effective), I am made to produce my appropriate result, I am set in operation, I am made to work. Mid. absent from N.T.

ἐπίγνωσις.s: ἐπίγνωσις, knowledge of a particular point (directed towards a particular object); perception, discernment, recognition; intuition.

μαρτύριον.s: μαρτύριον, witness, evidence (of recovery, Mt. viii 4, Mk. i 44, Lk. v 14: so of other occurrences or thoughts): ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, the tent of the congregation, the tent of meeting of God with His people, because it contained the ark and the tablets of the testimony to the covenant between God and his people, cf. Exod. xxv 9, 10.

ξύλον.s: ξύλον, wood, a piece of wood; hence, a club, a staff, Mk. xiv 43, 48 and parallels; the trunk of a tree, used to support the cross-bar of a cross in crucifixion, Ac. v 30, &c.; a tree, Lk. xxiii 31, ζωῆς, the fruit of which gives life, Rev. ii 7, xxii 2, 14, 19.

προάγω.s: προάγω, (a) tr. I lead forth, Ac. xvi 30; in the judicial sense, into court, Ac. xii 6, with ἐπί c. gen. of the person who is to try the case, Ac. xxv 26; (b) intr. and tr., I precede, I go before; so pres. pcpl. preceding, previous, Heb. vii 18; I lead forwards to a definite goal, 1 Tim. i 18; (c) intr., I go too far, 2 John 9.

σκηνή.s: σκηνή, a tent; a hut; usually with reference to the temporary abode of Yahweh, which preceded the Temple; ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, the tent as a witness to the covenant between God and His people: in Heb. ix the two parts of the one σκηνή, separated from one another by the curtain, are each called σκηνή.

σοφός.d: cf. sophomore, literally, a wise fool [μωρός]
σοφός.s: σοφός, wise: (Hebraism) skilled, an expert, a man of learning, Mt. xi 25, 1 Cor. iii 10, &c.

ὑψόω.d: cf. hypsophobia, fear of high places
ὑψόω.s: ὑψόω, I raise to a height, I lift up, I exalt, usually met.

ἀπέχω.g: I have received (payment); I am distant
ἀπέχω.s: ἀπέχω, (trans.) I have received (payment), a formula of receipts: so prob. also in Mk. xiv 41, ὁ Ἰούδας being understood as subject (there is hardly any other example in Greek of the meaning it is sufficient, but see Field ad loc.); (intrans.) I am away (distant) (from), of places and objects; (middle voice) I keep myself away (from), I refrain (from), I abstain (from).

γεωργός.s: γεωργός, a worker of the soil, husbandman, farmer, farm-labourer.

διακρίνω.s: διακρίνω, I separate, distinguish, discern one thing from another; διακρίνομαι, I doubt, hesitate, waver.

δῶρον.d: Theodore, Dorothea [or Dorothy], gift of God

ἐπάνω.s: ἐπάνω, (a) adv. on the top, above; (b) prep. on the top of, above, over, on: met. of rule, over, Lk. xix 17, &c.; above, more than, Mk. xiv 5, 1 Cor. xv 6.

ἐπιβάλλω.mg: to throw upon, impose, attack, fall to one
ἐπιβάλλω.s: ἐπιβάλλω, (a) I throw upon, cast over, 1 Cor. vii 35, Rev. xviii 19 (v.l.); (b) I place upon; (c) I lay, with τὴν χεῖρα (τὰς χεῖρας), either with innocent, or with hostile, intent (= inicere manum [manus]); (d) intr. I strike upon, Mk. iv 37; (e) intr. τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος, the share that falls to (belongs to) one, Lk. xv 12; (f) intr. ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν, he set to and wept, Mk. xiv 72.

ἐπιλαμβάνομαι.s: ἐπιλαμβάνομαι, I lay hold of, take hold of, seize (sometimes with beneficent, sometimes with hostile, intent).

ἐπουράνιος.s: ἐπουράνιος (opp. ἐπίγειος), heavenly, in heaven: ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις, in the heavenly sphere, the sphere of spiritual activities.

ἡγεμών.d: cf. hegemony, leadership, especially of one state of a confederacy
ἡγεμών.s: ἡγεμών (praeses, a very wide word), a (Roman) governor.

κοινωνία.s: κοινωνία, (lit. partnership) (a) contributory help, Ac. ii 42, Rom. xv 26, 2 Cor. viii 4, ix 13, Heb. xiii 16; (b) sharing in, Phil. i 5, iii 10, Philem. 6, cf. (c); (c) spiritual fellowship, a fellowship in the spirit, 1 Cor. i 9, x 16, 2 Cor. vi 14, xiii 13, Gal. ii 9, Phil. ii 1, 1 John i 3, 6, 7 (frequently outside N.T., of the marriage relationship).

κτίσις.s: κτίσις (often of the founding of a city), (a) abstr., creation; (b) concr., creation, creature, institution. Always of Divine work.

μεριμνάω.s: μεριμνάω, I am over-anxious; c. acc. I am anxious about, I care for.

μέχρι or μέχρις.g: until; with the gen., as far as
μέχρι or μέχρις.s: μέχρι, μέχρις, (conjunction) with or without οὗ, the ἄν (ἐάν) being omitted in N.T. examples, with aor. subj., until... shall have...: (preposition) as far as; until.

παλαιός.s: παλαιός, old; ὁ παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος (perhaps Hebraism), one’s former character (personality). The word and its derivatives bear a derogatory sense.

παρατίθημι.g: I set before; middle, I entrust
παρατίθημι.mg: to set before or beside, provide
παρατίθημι.s: παρατίθημι, (a) (adpono) I set (especially a meal) before, I serve; (b) (depono) act. and mid., I deposit with, I entrust to.

πότε.s: πότε, at what time?, when?: ἕως πότε, till what time?, till when?, how long? Also in indirect interrog. clauses.

προφητεία.s: προφητεία, the quality or action of a προφήτης, declaration of the will of God, whether with special reference to the future, in which case it may be translated prophecy, or not.

τέλειος.s: τέλειος (from τέλος, ‘final end’), (a) full-grown, mature, complete, having reached its utmost development, e.g. Eph. iv 13, Heb. v 14; (b) completely good (simply), James i 4; completely operative, James i 17; perfect, as dealing with universal principles, James i 25; perfect in character, Mt. v 48, James iii 2, &c.

τοσοῦτος.g: so great, so much; plural, so many
τοσοῦτος.mg: so great, so much, so many
τοσοῦτος.s: τοσοῦτος (tantus), so great, so large; of time, so long, plur. (tot, later tanti) so many: τοσούτου, at such and such a price, Ac. v 8.

τρέχω.s: τρέχω, I run; sometimes c. acc. of the course, Heb. xii 1: also met., e.g. Gal. ii 2.

ἀληθῶς.mg: truly, really, actually. ὡς ἀληθῶς same as ἀληθῶς

ἀνάγκη.s: ἀνάγκη, necessity, constraint, compulsion; ἔχω ἀνάγκην, I am obliged.

δέησις.s: δέησις, a requesting, a begging, request.

δεσμός.s: δεσμός, plur. sometimes δεσμά, a bond, chain; in Ac. xxiii 29, xxvi 31 (= uincula), the reference is to the form of ‘capital’ punishment involving loss of freedom and work in chains in the quarries.

ἐλέγχω.s: ἐλέγχω, (a) I reprove, rebuke: (b) I expose, show to be guilty, John iii 20, 1 Cor. xiv 24, Eph. v 11, 13, James ii 9.

θυμός.s: θυμός, an outburst of passion, wrath.

κατέχω.mg: to hold, check, seize, occupy, cease
κατέχω.s: κατέχω, (a) I hold fast, bind, arrest; (b) I take possession of, lay hold of, Lk. xiv 9; (c) I hold back, detain, restrain, Lk. iv 42, Rom. i 18, 2 Thess. ii 6, 7, Philem. 13; (d) I hold a ship (sc. τὴν ναῦν), keep its head, Ac. xxvii 40.

κενός.d: cenotaph, sepulchral monument to a person whose body is elsewhere
κενός.s: κενός, (a) empty; (b) met. empty (in moral content), vain, ineffective, foolish, worthless; εἰς κενόν, in vain, to no purpose; (c) false, unreal, pretentious, hollow, Eph. v 6, Col. ii 8, James ii 20.

κληρονομέω.s: κληρονομέω, I inherit, I obtain (possess) by inheritance.

κοιμάομαι.s: κοιμάομαι, I fall asleep, I am asleep, sometimes of the sleep of death (e.g. Mt. xxvii 52).

κόπος.s: κόπος, (a) trouble; κόπους (κόπον) τινι παρέχειν, to give trouble to one, to annoy one; (b) toil, labour, laborious toil, involving weariness and fatigue.

κρυπτός.s: κρυπτός, hidden, secret: τὰ κρυπτά, as subst. the hidden (secret) things (parts), the inward nature (character); ἐν [τῷ] κρυπτῷ, in the secret place, in the hidden sphere, inwardly.

μήν.d: menology, a calendar, especially that of the Greek Church, provided with short biographies of saints
μήν.mg: affirm. part., but, truly, indeed, forsooth, certainly

μήτι.g: interrogative particle, expecting a negative answer
μήτι.s: μήτι (μή strengthened by the addition of the acc. neut. of τις (indefinite) as adv.), (a) with εἰ: thus εἰ μήτι = εἰ μή, if not, unless, Lk. ix 13, εἰ μήτι ἄν, unless in a given case, 1 Cor. vii 5; (b) in questions, expecting a negative answer, cf. Mt. vii 16, can it be that? suggesting impossibility.

οἰκοδομή.s: οἰκοδομή, (a) abstract, building, the operation (process) of building, sometimes transitional, without being strictly concrete, 1 Cor. iii 9, 2 Cor. v 1, Eph. ii 21, iv 12, 16, 29 (here perhaps = improvement); met. upbuilding, edification; (b) concrete, a building, Mk. xiii 1, 2, Mt. xxiv 1.

προστίθημι.s: προστίθημι (addo), I place (put) to, I add: mid. c. infin. (perhaps a Hebraistic idiom), best translated by representing the verb in the infinitive by the indicative, and adding the word besides, &c., thus:—προσέθετο πέμψαι, besides (in addition, further) he sent, Lk. xx 11.

πυλών.s: πυλών (properly, the passage which led from the street through the front part of the house to the inner court, closed by a heavy πύλη at the streetward end), entrance passage, gateway; gate.

στέφανος.s: στέφανος, a garland, wreath, chaplet, crown, generally as the Greek victor’s crown or chaplet, of perishable leaves (1 Cor. ix 25), won in athletic and other contests, and familiar to the Jews for generations: ὁ στέφανος τῆς ζωῆς (James i 12, Rev. ii 10), the crown (reward), which is life.

τίκτω.s: τίκτω (of a woman), I bear, give birth to, bring forth: hence met., of the earth, Heb. vi 7, of evil desire, James i 15.

ὑποκριτής.s: ὑποκριτής (properly an actor), a hypocrite, one who outwardly plays the part of a religious man to perfection, but is inwardly alien to the spirit of true religion.

ὑπομένω.s: ὑπομένω, (a) I remain behind, Lk. ii 43, Ac. xvii 14; (b) absolutely, I stand my ground, I show endurance, Mt. x 22, &c.; with τῇ θλίψει, Rom. xii 12, in persecution, amid persecution, with εἰς = ἐν, Heb. xii 7; (c) tr. I endure, bear up against.

φανερός.s: φανερός, clear, visible (as opposed to ‘hidden’, ‘secret’); εἰς φανερὸν ἐλθεῖν, to come into the open, to appear before the public, Mk. iv 22, Lk. viii 17, ἐν τῷ φανερῷ, in public.

ἀρέσκω.s: ἀρέσκω, I please, with the idea of willing service rendered to others; hence almost I serve.

αὐτοῦ.s: ἑαυτοῦ, &c., self, selves; for all three persons, singular (not first person) and plural, according to context, ourselves; yourself, yourselves; himself, herself, itself, themselves.

ἄφεσις.d: aphesis, the gradual loss of a short unaccented vowel at the beginning of a word; as 'squire' for 'esquire'
ἄφεσις.s: ἄφεσις (from ἀφίημι) (remissio), a sending away, a letting go, a release; hence (cf. in inscriptions, remission from debt or punishment), remission, forgiveness.

γάμος.d: bigamy, double marriage; digamy, second marriage after the decease of the first spouse, condemned as a sin by certain Church Fathers
γάμος.s: γάμος, a marriage, wedding, wedding-ceremony: γάμοι (plur.), a wedding-feast.

δέσμιος.s: δέσμιος, bound, captive, in chains; sometimes substantivally prisoner, captive.

εἰσπορεύομαι.s: εἰσπορεύομαι, I journey in(to), I go in(to).

ἑκατόν.d: hecatomb, great public sacrifice, properly of 100 oxen [βοῦς]
ἑκατόν.s: ἑκατόν, a hundred; εἰς ἑκατόν, see εἰς.

ἐξίστημι.s: ἐξίστημι, ἐξιστάω, ἐξιστάνω (lit. I remove from a standing position), (a) in tr. tenses (including ἐξέστᾰκα), I astonish, amaze; (b) in intr. tenses, I am astonished, amazed; I am out of my mind, I am mad, Mk. iii 21, 2 Cor. v 13.

ἐπιμένω.s: ἐπιμένω, (a) I remain, tarry; (b) c. dat. I remain in, persist in.

θησαυρός.s: θησαυρός, a store-house for precious things; hence a treasure, a store.

καθάπερ.s: καθάπερ (i. e. καθ’ ἅπερ, according to which things), even as.

καταλύω.s: καταλύω (lit. I loosen thoroughly), (a) tr. I break up, overthrow, destroy, both lit. and met., ὁ καταλύων, you would-be destroyer (of), Mt. xxvii 40; (b) I unyoke, unharness a carriage horse or pack animal; hence I put up, I lodge, I find a lodging, Lk. ix 12, xix 7.

κερδαίνω.s: κερδαίνω, I gain: ὕβριν καὶ ζημίαν, I gain injury and loss, i.e. I gain by shunning injury and loss, I do not suffer (I am spared) injury and loss, Ac. xxvii 21.

νίπτω.s: νίπτω, I wash; mid. I wash my own (hands, &c.).

νυμφίος.s: νυμφίος, a bridegroom: name applied to the Messiah, Mk. ii 19, 20 and parallels.

περιτέμνω.s: περιτέμνω (circumcido), I cut round the foreskin, I circumcise.

πέτρα.s: πέτρα, rock, solid rock, native rock, rising up through the earth, which trips up the traveller, Rom. ix 33, 1 Pet. ii 8; in Mt. xvi 18, of such faith as Peter has just shown; in 1 Cor. x 4, allegorically interpreted.

πλήρωμα.d: pleroma, in Valentinian Gnosticism, the world of light, including the body of eons
πλήρωμα.s: πλήρωμα (indicates the result of the activity denoted by πληρόω), (a) a fill, fullness; full complement; supply, supplement, Mk. ii 21, Mt. ix 16; (b) fullness, filling, fulfilment, completion.

πλησίον.g: near; as a noun, a neighbor
πλησίον.s: πλησίον, adv. (near, John iv 5), used as adj. and (especially with article ὁ) noun, neighbouring, neighbourly; a neighbour.

ποιμήν.s: ποιμήν, a shepherd: hence met., of the feeder, protector, and ruler of a flock of men.

ῥύομαι.s: ῥύομαι, I rescue (from danger or destruction).

σκοτία.d: scotoscope, a fieldglass for seeing by night
σκοτία.s: σκοτία, darkness: hence met. of ignorance and sin.

χάρισμα.d: charism, a special spiritual gift or power divinely conferred; I Cor. 12
χάρισμα.s: χάρισμα, a free (gracious) gift, a gift, an endowment, especially from God.

ὡσαύτως.s: ὡσαύτως, in the same way, likewise.

ἀνακρίνω.mg: to examine well; mid. question one with another
ἀνακρίνω.s: ἀνακρίνω, I examine, inquire into (judicially: see ἀνάκρισις); of the preliminary examination, preceding the trial proper: hence with derived applications.

ἀπάγω.s: ἀπάγω, I lead away, [for example (=duco) I lead away to execution, Ac. xii 19]; hence, in the moral sphere, 1 Cor. xii 2; also, of a road leading to a place.

δεῖπνον.s: δεῖπνον, a dinner, an afternoon or evening meal.

δηνάριον.s: δηνάριον, a denarius, a small Roman silver coin, weighing in Nero's time 53 grs. Its value and purchasing power varied from time to time.

ἐκχέω.s: ἐκχέω, I pour out (liquid or solid), I shed. See ἐκχύννω.

ἐντέλλομαι.s: ἐντέλλομαι, I give orders (injunctions, instructions, commands).

ἐπιθυμέω.s: ἐπιθυμέω, I desire, long; ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπιθυμεῖν, Hebraistic, to long eagerly, Lk. xxii 15.

ἐργάτης.s: ἐργάτης, a field-labourer; then, a labourer, workman in general.

ζῆλος.s: ζῆλος (masc. and neut.), (a) eagerness, zeal, enthusiasm; (b) jealousy, rivalry.

θεμέλιος.s: θεμέλιος (properly an adj. belonging to the foundation, with λίθος understood), a foundation stone; plur. neut. θεμέλια is used, Ac. xvi 26.

κακῶς.s: κακῶς, badly, evilly: κακῶς ἔχω, see ἔχω.

κατέρχομαι.s: κατέρχομαι, I come down from sky to earth, or from high land to lower land (or to the coast), or from the high seas to the shore: pcpl. qualitative in James iii 15.

πάθημα.s: πάθημα, properly colourless, an experience: but most commonly, an evil experience, evil treatment, suffering, e.g. τὰ εἰς Χριστὸν παθήματα, the sufferings destined for Messiah, 1 Pet. i 11.

παρέχω.s: παρέχω, act. and mid. I offer, provide, confer, afford, give, bring, show, cause: κόπους (κόπον) τινὶ παρέχειν, to cause one trouble.

πληρής.s: πλήρης (sometimes, from about the beginning of our era, indeclinable, and used for any case singular or plural, a usage perhaps derived from commercial life: e.g. Mk. iv 28 (?), John i 14, where πλήρης agrees with δόξαν, and there should be no parenthesis, Ac. vi 5 (v.l.)), full.

πολεμός.s: πόλεμος, a war; also, a battle, Lk. xiv 31, &c.

προσδοκάω.s: προσδοκάω, I expect, wait for, await.

ῥαββεί or ῥαββί.s: ραββεί (Aramaic), my master, a title given by pupils to their teacher.

ῥίζα.s: ῥίζα, a root: hence met., a source.

συκῆ.d: sycophant, a flatterer, literally, a fig-shower [the reason for the name is not definitely known]

συλλαμβάνω.s: συλλαμβάνω (συνλ-), (a) (conprehendo) act. and mid., I arrest, catch, capture: (b) I conceive (a child), cf. met. James i 15; (c) mid. I lend a hand to, I help, Lk. v 7, Phil. iv 3.

συνίστημι or συνιστάνω.g: transitive tenses, I commend; intransitive tenses, I stand with, consist
συνίστημι or συνιστάνω.s: συνίστημι, συνιστάνω, (a) in transitive tenses, (1) I recommend, commend, introduce, Rom. xvi 1, 2 Cor. iii 1, iv 2, v 12, vi 4, x 12, 18, xii 11; (2) I show, prove, Rom. iii 5, v 8, 2 Cor. vii 11, Gal. ii 18; (b) in intransitive tenses, (1) I stand with (by), Lk. ix 32; (2) I consist, I am held together, Col. i 17, 2 Pet. iii 5.

σφραγίς.d: sphragistics, the science of seals, their history, age, distinctions, etc.
σφραγίς.s: σφραγίς, a seal, a means not merely of attestation but also of closing, so that a cabinet, document, &c., could not be opened without breaking the seals.

τέρας.s: τέρας, a prodigy, an extraordinary occurrence (appearance, act), a startling portent.

τολμάω.s: τολμάω, I have courage, I dare, I have the hardihood; I take courage, Mk. xv 43; I submit to, Rom. v 7.

τροφή.d: cf. atrophy, wasting due to malnutrition

ὑστερέω.mg: to come later than, be inferior to
ὑστερέω.s: ὑστερέω, (a) act. intr. I come late, I am late, Heb. iv 1; I am left behind in the race for, I have no part in, with ἀπό and the gen. of the end, Heb. xii 15; I fall short, I am inferior, Mt. xix 20, 1 Cor. xii 24 (v. l.), 2 Cor. xi 5, xii 11; I am wanting (to), Mk. x 21 (v. l.), John ii 3; I am without, c. gen. Lk. xxii 35; (b) pass. I suffer from want, absol., or c. gen., or c. ἐν and dat.; I am worse off (for honour), 1 Cor. viii 8.

χορτάζω.g: I eat to the full, am satisfied, am filled
χορτάζω.s: χορτάζω (sagino) (from χόρτος, in earlier Greek of feeding animals), I feed to the full, I satisfy with food.

ὦ.s: ὦ, an interjection of address, O.

ἀνέχομαι.s: ἀνέχομαι, I endure (in 2 Thess. i 4, and Mt. vi 24=Lk. xvi 13, text doubtful).

γυμνός.s: γυμνός, rarely stark-naked, generally wearing only the under-garment (χιτών), see γυμνιτεύω; γυμνὸς κόκκος, a simple seed, a seed per se.

διαμαρτύρομαι.s: διαμαρτύρομαι, I give solemn evidence, I testify (declare) solemnly.

ἐλαία.s: ἐλαία (olea), an olive tree: see ἐλαίων.

ἐπαγγέλλομαι.s: ἐπαγγέλλομαι, (a) I promise; (b) I profess, 1 Tim. ii 10, vi 21.

καταλαμβάνω.mg: to seize upon, occupy, overtake, catch
